newsitem.title: UK: Thailand, Brazil cited in new sugar freight orders.
newsitem.headline: Thailand, Brazil cited in new sugar freight orders.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh business on Tuesday with Thailand and Brazil dominating as quoted origins, shipbrokers said.
CSR quoted for 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for June 25/July 5 and Louis Dreyfus was open for 12,000 tonnes from Thailand to south China for June 20/25.
Jean Lion launched two bulk orders, quoting for 24/25,000 tonnes from Cuba to Morocco/Black Sea/Baltic for any June dates and 13,000 tonnes from Thailand to Pakistan for seven days notice.

Cargill issued a replacement order for 22,800 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to Black Sea/Baltic/Med for prompt shipment and was said to have fixed 10,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to Lagos for early June.
Sucre Export was open for 13/13,650 tonnes of bagged sugar from south China to Pakistan/Red Sea for mid-June.

Of the day's other firmer business, shipbrokers said Genoc was thought to be on subjects with a prompt 13/14,000-tonne bagged cargo from Poland to Mediterranean with options of Red Sea and Indian Ocean.
Dreyfus fixed 12/14,000 tonnnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Pakistan and Kerry 13,500 tonnes in bulk from Thailand to south China, they said.
